segments.arabic:
١٢٠٢٥- أم رعلة»
: بكسر أوله وسكون المهملة، القشيريّة. لها حديث
أورده المستغفريّ، من طريق، وأبو موسى من طريق آخر، كلاهما من حديث ابن عبّاس- أن امرأة يقال لها رعلة القشيريّة وفدت على النّبيّ ﷺ، وكانت امرأة ذات لسان وفصاحة، فقالت:
السلام عليك يا رسول اللَّه ورحمة اللَّه وبركاته، إنا ذوات الخدور، ومحل أزر البعول، ومربيات الأولاد، ولا حظّ لنا في الجيش، فعلّمنا شيئا يقربنا إلى اللَّه ﷿. فقال:
«عليكنّ بذكر اللَّه آناء اللّيل وأطراف النّهار، وغضّ البصر، وخفض الصّوت ...» الحديث، وفيه: قالت: يا رسول اللَّه، إني امرأة مقيّنة أقيّن النساء وأزينهنّ لأزواجهن، فهل هو حوب فأثبّط عنه؟ فقال لها: يا أم رعلة: «قيّنيهنّ وزيّنيهنّ إذا كسدن» .
ثم غابت حياة رسول اللَّه ﷺ وأقبلت في أيام الردة، فذكر لها قصّة في الحزن على النّبيّ ﵌ وتطوافها بالحسن والحسين أزقّة المدينة تبكي عليه، وأنشد لها مرثية منها:
يا دار فاطمة المعمور ساحتها ... هيّجت لي حزنا حيّيت من دار
[البسيط] قال أبو موسى- بعد سياقه هذا الإسناد: لا يحتمل هذا، والحمل فيه على أبي القاسم جعفر بن محمد بن إبراهيم السرندسي «٢»، فإنه غير مشهور، ولا هو مذكور في رجال أصبهان، ثم ساق من طريق عبد اللَّه بن محمد البلويّ، عن عمارة بن زيد، عن إبراهيم بن سعد، عن ابن إسحاق، عن يحيى بن عبد اللَّه بن الحارث بن نوفل، عن أبيه، عن ابن عبّاس، قال: قدمت القشيريّة مع زوجها أبي رعلة وكانت امرأة بدويّة ذات لسان فكان النبيّ ﵌ بها معجبا.
فذكر نحوه، وقال في آخر الحديث: فهاجت المدينة مأتما، فلم يبق دار من دور الأنصار إلا وأهلها يبكون. قال أبو موسى: هذا الإسناد أليق بهذا الحديث، يعني لشهرة البلويّ بالكذب. واللَّه أعلم.
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٤٤٨) .
(٢) في أالسر بديني.
segments.english:
12025 — Umm Ri'la(1):

With kasra on its first letter and sukun on the unpointed 'ayn; she was of Qushayr. She had a hadith that al-Mustaghfiri cited through one route and Abu Musa through another, both from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: A woman called Ri'la al-Qushayriyya came as a delegate to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She was a woman gifted with speech and eloquence. She said:

“Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and Allah's mercy and blessings. We are women of the curtained chambers, the resting places of our husbands' waist-wraps, and the raisers of children, and we have no share in the army. Teach us something that will bring us nearer to Allah, Glorious and Exalted.” He said:

“You must remember Allah during the hours of the night and at the ends of the day, lower your gaze, and lower your voices…” to the end of the hadith. In it, she said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am a beautician: I beautify women and adorn them for their husbands. Is that a sin, such that I should desist from it?” He said to her: “O Umm Ri'la, beautify and adorn them when they are no longer sought after.”

She then remained absent for the rest of the Messenger of Allah's lifetime and reappeared during the days of the Apostasy. A story was then recounted of her grief for the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and of her going around the alleys of Medina with al-Hasan and al-Husayn, weeping for him. An elegy by her was cited, including:

O abode of Fatima, whose courtyard is flourishing,
You have stirred grief in me; may you be greeted as an abode.

[Basit meter]

After setting forth this chain of transmission, Abu Musa said: “This is untenable, and the blame for it falls on Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarandasi(2), for he is not well known, nor is he mentioned among the men of Isfahan.” He then transmitted by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi, from 'Umara ibn Zayd, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: “The Qushayri woman came with her husband, Abu Ri'la. She was a Bedouin woman gifted with speech, and the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—admired her.”

He then related a similar account and said at the end of the hadith: “Medina was roused to mourning, and no house among the houses of the Ansar remained without its inhabitants weeping.” Abu Musa said: “This chain is more fitting for this hadith”—meaning because al-Balawi was notorious for lying. Allah knows best.

(1) Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7448.

(2) In manuscript A: al-Sarbadini.

names.english: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sarbadini

unresolved.explanation: The expression invokes something becoming unsought or lacking demand. The canonical wording does not safely establish whether the intended reference is specifically loss of a husband's interest, lack of suitors, or diminished desirability more generally; the translation therefore retains the broad sense “when they are no longer sought after.”

Manuscript A's variant is preserved as al-Sarbadini, but the supplied evidence does not securely establish its spacing or vocalization. It is a spelling variant of al-Sarandasi, not a separate person.
